authority: Generated executable projection. Edit _validation_registry.json, then run npm run validation:matrix.

lineage_policy.authority: _validation_registry.json is the executable source of truth for validation selection, dependency order, prerequisites, outputs, severity, and mutation boundaries.
lineage_policy.dependency_rule: Dependencies are included recursively and executed in topological order before dependents.
lineage_policy.prerequisite_rule: Missing required files trigger registered prepare_commands. Unregistered preparation is forbidden.
lineage_policy.mutation_rule: Validator commands may write only declared mutates_files. Source roots are hash-checked before and after each validator.
lineage_policy.output_rule: Declared produces_files must exist after a passing validator.

HARD_FAIL.meaning: Direct production, user-safety, evidence, route, workflow, build, or delivery threat; never cosmetic formatting.

STRONG_WARNING.meaning: Material quality, ingestion, indexing, accessibility, or performance degradation.

SOFT_WARNING.meaning: Maintainability, documentation, style, or low-risk quality concern.

INFO.meaning: Metric, observation, historical evidence, or optimization note.

scope_definitions.CONTAINER: Runnable in the standard container without provider credentials.
scope_definitions.LOCAL_ONLY: Requires deployed URL, browser runtime, credentials, or operator environment.

core.description: Pure default release-blocking checks; no mutation and no external provider dependency.

release.description: Full container release proof: core plus source immutability, hygiene, and deterministic build.

strict.description: Release proof plus advisory checks; warnings remain visible but do not block.

advisory.description: Non-blocking quality and ingestion warnings only.

local.description: Full release proof plus deployed Playwright click audit.

audit.description: Collect-all execution of every active and on-demand validator; local-only checks are deferred unless explicitly enabled.

social.description: Public-signal normalization and candidate loop validation.

llm.description: LLM export, answer-block, entity-graph, and citation-target validation.

homepages.description: Homepage-only schema and assistance boundary checks.

canonical-data.description: Protected canonical source static and runtime immutability checks.

postrelease.description: Pure post-build structural verification; no content release or mutation.

content-release.description: Lean content-release checks for generated static content and routing contracts.

agent-run.description: Agent artifact ingestion, FIX compilation, exact implementation, and semantic acceptance proof.

full-audit.description: Hostile collect-all review of all active validators without pretending every advisory check belongs in core.

citation-intelligence.description: Traffic-qualified citation intelligence, proof packet, atom, structural graph, and workflow topology gates.

deep-isolated.description: Isolated deep container validation: workflow data trace, browserless mock backup, and traffic-qualified citation intelligence only. No real browser claim.

HARD_FAIL.title: Pages carry the blocks the review agent keeps requesting
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Across ~2,750 external review recommendations in this repo and sprylabs, the agent asks for the same small set of blocks. 27% of distinct defects were re-reported on later runs despite being marked released - one across 8 run dates. Without a pre-publish check, new pages ship missing the same blocks and the loop repeats. Blocking checks cover the four that decide whether a page can be quoted or converted at all: direct answer, a heading carrying the query, no empty table cells, and one conversion path. The rest report as coverage gaps so a backlog is visible without stopping a release.

HARD_FAIL.title: Published pages contain no internal build instructions

Two generator paths rendered them as reader-facing copy - a fallback acceptance-checklist card, and target.answer via 'Citation-ready update: '. 163 published pages carried the first and 100 the second, the latter inside the direct-answer block that answer engines extract. It also caused the external agent to re-flag pages marked released, because it was reading its own instruction back off the page.

HARD_FAIL.title: Generators refuse internal build instructions at source
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: no-internal-instruction-leak scans published HTML, so it fires only after a generator has already written a build directive into a page, on whatever run happens to rebuild it. a5bd62cc8 removed the two known render sites, added looksLikeInternalInstruction() to agent_exact_repairs.js and never called it, and never touched the compiler; html_fix_acceptance_parser.js went on lifting an agent's quoted example of the defect into an artifact title and a required_string, which is how insights/neuro-013 shipped an <h2> reading 'Citation-ready update: FILEPATH...'. This asserts both producers import the shared predicate and call it, and that the gate's pattern set and the generator's refusal set cannot drift apart.

HARD_FAIL.title: Citation-occupancy probe contract
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Prevents a narrow occupancy run from silently DELETING the readings a wider run paid to take (--merge exists but neither caller passed it; 169 of 205 measured readings were destroyed by one scheduled refresh). Prevents "unbranded" reverting to a blind fallthrough in which foreign government, health-service and regulator hosts count as citation slots an independent microsite can hold. Prevents an occupancy reading being published with no blue_ocean_eligible gate, i.e. "not cited" read as "open ground". Fails if it examines zero probes.

HARD_FAIL.title: Citation-occupancy control separation and open-bucket integrity
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: Makes the occupancy probe's own control pair binding. FAILS the run when the pair INVERTS - the query known to be CLOSED measuring more open than the one known to be OPEN, which is what happened (1.00 against 0.50) while the check was only a printed note and five pages were queued for publication off the numbers it did not stop. Re-classifies every recorded citation host with the shared classifier and FAILS if any unrecognised host is counted as open, or if a recorded open/unclassifiable count does not match what the hosts derive. FAILS if a citation_occupancy number is published while the controls do not separate, or withheld while they do. Requires the unclassifiable slot count on every run. Hard-fails if it examines zero probes, zero cited hosts or zero controls.

HARD_FAIL.title: Social fallback backlog depth must be reported honestly
HARD_FAIL.risk_prevented: social_fallback_suppressed_count is bounded by the run's remaining capacity, so on any run where agent artifacts fill the daily target it reports 0 while a real eligible backlog sits unreleased. Measured on current data the true depth is 389 against a suppressed_count of 68. A human reading the plan then believes nothing is being held back. Suppressing social fallback is a deliberate contract-enforced policy and is not challenged here; only the honesty of the reported number is enforced.

Tier 1.title: Citation-occupancy probe contract
Tier 1.risk_prevented: Prevents a narrow occupancy run from silently DELETING the readings a wider run paid to take (--merge exists but neither caller passed it; 169 of 205 measured readings were destroyed by one scheduled refresh). Prevents "unbranded" reverting to a blind fallthrough in which foreign government, health-service and regulator hosts count as citation slots an independent microsite can hold. Prevents an occupancy reading being published with no blue_ocean_eligible gate, i.e. "not cited" read as "open ground". Fails if it examines zero probes.

Tier 1.title: Citation-occupancy control separation and open-bucket integrity
Tier 1.risk_prevented: Makes the occupancy probe's own control pair binding. FAILS the run when the pair INVERTS - the query known to be CLOSED measuring more open than the one known to be OPEN, which is what happened (1.00 against 0.50) while the check was only a printed note and five pages were queued for publication off the numbers it did not stop. Re-classifies every recorded citation host with the shared classifier and FAILS if any unrecognised host is counted as open, or if a recorded open/unclassifiable count does not match what the hosts derive. FAILS if a citation_occupancy number is published while the controls do not separate, or withheld while they do. Requires the unclassifiable slot count on every run. Hard-fails if it examines zero probes, zero cited hosts or zero controls.

Tier 1.title: Social fallback backlog depth must be reported honestly
Tier 1.risk_prevented: social_fallback_suppressed_count is bounded by the run's remaining capacity, so on any run where agent artifacts fill the daily target it reports 0 while a real eligible backlog sits unreleased. Measured on current data the true depth is 389 against a suppressed_count of 68. A human reading the plan then believes nothing is being held back. Suppressing social fallback is a deliberate contract-enforced policy and is not challenged here; only the honesty of the reported number is enforced.

Tier 3.title: Pages carry the blocks the review agent keeps requesting
Tier 3.risk_prevented: Across ~2,750 external review recommendations in this repo and sprylabs, the agent asks for the same small set of blocks. 27% of distinct defects were re-reported on later runs despite being marked released - one across 8 run dates. Without a pre-publish check, new pages ship missing the same blocks and the loop repeats. Blocking checks cover the four that decide whether a page can be quoted or converted at all: direct answer, a heading carrying the query, no empty table cells, and one conversion path. The rest report as coverage gaps so a backlog is visible without stopping a release.

Tier 6.risk_prevented: Degraded Reddit or public-signal intake can reduce query discovery coverage.

Tier 6.title: Four-layer strategy authority and anti-fabrication integrity
Tier 6.risk_prevented: The repository could contradict its publishing authority, expose unverified provider or reviewer data, or publish an unsupported sameAs graph while technical validators still pass.

Tier 5.title: Velocity-to-canonical routing law
Tier 5.risk_prevented: Velocity pages could ship without a real link to the correct canonical destination or without top/bottom routing boundaries.

Tier 5.title: Demand-backed page admission
Tier 5.risk_prevented: A sitemap URL can point at nothing, a rendered route can reach no public surface, and the admitted corpus can grow on fan-out planning records rather than on a query with measured volume.

Tier 5.title: Executable-file permissions
Tier 5.risk_prevented: Required shell or executable scripts may become unusable after extraction.

Tier 5.title: Network identity and crawler access contract
Tier 5.risk_prevented: Search crawlers could be blocked or rendered pages could lose truthful network identity; training-bot access remains an explicit publisher choice.

Tier 5.title: Public inventory contract
Tier 5.risk_prevented: Unexpected, quarantined, or missing routes could enter the release.

Tier 5.title: Rendered hierarchy integrity
Tier 5.risk_prevented: Atlas, cluster, and insight pages can be missing, thin, or disconnected.

Tier 5.title: Rendered href and asset integrity
Tier 5.risk_prevented: Broken internal links or assets create user and crawler failures.

Tier 5.title: Indexable HTML search-quality fundamentals
Tier 5.risk_prevented: Indexable pages could ship with mojibake, missing metadata, invalid heading structure, admitted redirect aliases, or exact duplicate content.

Tier 5.title: Sitemap and inventory parity
Tier 5.risk_prevented: Published pages can become undiscoverable or stale URLs can remain indexed.

Tier 5.title: Public route, browser assertion, and click-audit parity
Tier 5.risk_prevented: A declared browser suite can drift from the runner, route manifest, CTA labels, or representative state-page families.

Tier 5.title: GitHub Actions trigger, data, secret, artifact, and manual-run trace
Tier 5.risk_prevented: Manual or scheduled workflows can fail after deployment because triggers, variables, artifacts, or runtime prerequisites drift.

Tier 8.title: Deterministic build comparison
Tier 8.risk_prevented: Identical source could generate different public output or freshness churn.

Tier 8.title: Deployed public click audit
Tier 8.risk_prevented: Static validation cannot prove real HTTP, console, viewport, and navigation behavior.

Tier 8.title: Repository and packaging hygiene
Tier 8.risk_prevented: Logs, nested repos, generated junk, or backup artifacts can contaminate the baseline ZIP.
